newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P rates Countrywide Corp US$150 mln FRNs 'A'.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Countrywide Corp US$150 mln FRNs 'A'.

text.p: Standard and Poor's on Tuesday said it had assigned an 'A' rating to the US$150 million floating rate notes issued by Countrywide Corporation Ltd (CCL), based on the guarantee provided by parent Countrywide Banking Corp Ltd in New Zealand.
S&P said the rating outlook was stable.

S&P said it rated Countrywide A/A-1, reflecting Countrywide's 100 percent ownership by Bank of Scotland rated A+/A-1, together with Countrywide's own strong profile, its good asset quality, and sound underlying profitability.
S&P said this issue was being sold predominantly into the Hong Kong market.
Countrywide is a relatively small retail bank operating in the New Zealand market, with assets totalling NZ$6.483 billion at February 1996, S&P said.
"Standard & Poor's considers Countrywide's credit policies to be conservative, which should ensure that credit quality is maintained," S&P said.

The ratings agency said it expected the competitive environment in New Zealand to moderate income and asset growth, "however, continuing focus on overhead costs and efficiency of distribution is expected to result in stable profits, going forward." -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
